packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-04 -- unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this text. I read only BRIEF.md, PROMPT.md and the packet images (plus crops I made of them).

LAYOUT SURVEY

Face A (overview image-001.jpg; tiles image-002..013, a 3-column x 4-row grid of native-resolution tiles that overlap their neighbours)
- Single parchment leaf, portrait, photographed flat on black with ruler at top and colour checker at lower right. A grey rectangle (redaction/label mask) covers an area at lower right of the text block.
- Leaf is heavily creased and stained; a strip at the top is folded over / torn (a loose parchment strip loops above the top edge). Fold lines visible vertically near left and right edges and horizontally at mid-height, consistent with use as a wrapper/cover.
- A later inscription in large dark ink (German Kurrent/Fraktur-style display hand) sits across the upper part: a date line "1 5 8[?]" and below it two lines, read from the overview as roughly "Büechhaimer ausgaben / vnd Einnemmen[?] etc." (to be checked on tiles).
- Under it, a much fainter, abraded earlier text block in a single wide column, many lines of small script, mostly very faded. Ruled margins visible (vertical lines at left ~x=300 and ~x=390 in overview, right edge ~x=970).
- Upside-down / folded-over text along the top strip (line of script visible at y~290 in the overview, reads as a line of the underlying text on the folded flap, possibly inverted).
- Modern pencil shelfmark lower centre: "Stams, StA, Frg. 194r" (as it appears; last character uncertain). Pencil number at right margin around y~830 ("2?").
- Interpretation (tentative): later archival wrapper title written over an erased or faded earlier manuscript text.

Face B (overview image-014.jpg; tiles image-015..026, same 3 x 4 grid: 015-017 top row, 018-020, 021-023, 024-026 bottom row; left/centre/right)
- Same leaf, other side; same outline and fold pattern (mirror). Pencil shelfmark at bottom centre: "Stams, StA, Frg. 194v" (as it appears).
- Single block of long lines running the full width of the leaf (no columns), about 40 lines, in a German cursive (Kurrent-type) documentary hand, brown ink. Text ends about two-thirds down; lower third blank.
- First line opens with a large decorated/cadelled initial "W" at upper left and the opening words written in an enlarged display script: "Wir Johannes Abbt vnnd Regierennder Prelat des wirdigen G..." (as read from overview; checked on tiles below).
- Right margin carries several marginal additions/notes in the same or a similar cursive hand, keyed to lines in the middle of the text (roughly lines 10-30), some running down a narrow strip at the right edge.
- Some lines show insertions above the line. Heavy staining and creasing on the left and centre-left; text at the left margin and at the folds is partly lost.
- Interpretation (tentative): a German-language document (charter/deed type) issued in the first person plural by an abbot, with descriptions of lands and boundaries (words like "Item", "hof", "acker", "gelegen", "stosst" are visible in overview). I do not identify it further.
- Because each physical line runs across three tiles (left, centre, right), I transcribe each tile row as left/centre/right segments with tile line numbers; joins between tiles are marked "//".

READING ORDER CHOSEN: Face B tiles first (the legible text), then Face A tiles as far as the image limit allows.


======================================================================
FACE B TRANSCRIPTION
Conventions: line numbers count from the top of each tile image. "/" = virgule as written. (..) = proposed expansion. "?" after a word = uncertain. Line beginnings at the left edge are partly lost to creasing/stain. u/v and i/j kept as written where clear.
